newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Selling in Telecom sends NZ shares to weaker close.
newsitem.headline: Selling in Telecom sends NZ shares to weaker close.

text.p: * Telecom weakness accounts for over half of index fall
* Brierley unchanged after Thistle float details
Weakness in market leader Telecom pushed New Zealand shares to a lower close on Thursday, with the NZSE-40 capital index shedding 23.03 points or one percent to 2,212.22.
"The market was pretty soggy," said Ian Waddell at Hendry Hay McIntosh.
Telecom fell 15 cents to $6.80 and accounted for 13 points of the overall index fall, which was on moderate market volume of $46 million.
Waddell said a large offshore buyer who had been active for some time in Telecom was absent from the market today. It was a similar story with Fletcher Energy, down 10 cents to $3.44.
ANZ Securities Managing Director Tim Preston said the market was predictably tentative on the eve of the Reserve Bank Economic Projections due on Friday at 9 a.m. (2100 GMT Thursday).

He said there were few apparent surprises in Treasury's pre-election economic and fiscal update, released after the market closed, which predicted a gradual easing in monetary conditions from the December 1996 quarter.

Preston said there was some initial selling in Brierley Investments after the announcement of a rather lower than expected price range for shares in British hotel group Thistle, which is 70 percent owned by BIL. The stock came back to close unchanged at $1.43. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
